questions.question: A shipping system records that a particular SUPPLIER delivered a particular PART to a particular PROJECT; no pair of the three entities alone captures a delivery. What is this relationship type called?
questions.explanation: Because the association requires SUPPLIER, PART, and PROJECT to participate simultaneously, it is a ternary (degree-3) relationship; splitting it into binaries loses the three-way fact.

questions.question: A design team drops ER diagrams entirely and documents each entity as a class with typed attributes, associations, and multiplicities — using the same notation they already use for object-oriented code. Which notation are they using?
questions.explanation: UML class diagrams model classes (entities) with attributes and associations with multiplicities, and are a common alternative notation to ER diagrams for conceptual data modeling.

questions.question: Starting from the generic EMPLOYEE entity type, the designer adds the subtype entities SECRETARY, TECHNICIAN, and ENGINEER, each carrying attributes the supertype lacks. Which top-down EER process created these subtypes?
questions.explanation: Specialization refines a superclass into subtypes top-down; the reverse process, generalization, abstracts shared entity types bottom-up into a superclass.

questions.question: In the specialization PERSON → {STUDENT, EMPLOYEE}, the business rule states that no person may appear in both subtype lists. Which specialization constraint enforces this rule?
questions.explanation: A disjoint specialization restricts each supertype instance to membership in at most one subtype; here a person is either a student or an employee, never both.

questions.question: In the specialization PERSON → {STUDENT, STAFF}, the rules permit a teaching assistant to appear in both subtype lists at the same time. Which specialization constraint applies?
questions.explanation: An overlapping specialization allows a supertype instance to belong to several subtypes simultaneously, unlike the disjoint case.

questions.question: On an EER diagram the designer must decide whether every EMPLOYEE must appear in HOURLY or SALARIED (total) or may remain unclassified (partial). Which category of specialization constraint is being decided?
questions.explanation: The completeness constraint specifies whether specialization is total (every supertype instance must join a subtype) or partial (membership optional); it is independent of the disjoint/overlap decision.

questions.question: The relationship MANAGES links an EMPLOYEE who supervises to an EMPLOYEE who is supervised — both participations belong to the same entity type. What is this relationship type called?
questions.explanation: When the same entity type participates more than once in different roles within one relationship, it is a recursive (unary) relationship.

questions.question: After the ER diagram is approved, the team systematically creates one base table per strong entity, then handles weak entities, relationships, and multivalued attributes until a relational schema exists. Which design step did they just perform?
questions.explanation: ER-to-relational mapping is the algorithmic step that converts entity types, relationship types, and attributes of an ER model into relational tables and keys.

questions.question: DEPENDENT is a weak entity owned by EMPLOYEE. A dependent row becomes identifiable only when Emp_ssn is combined with the Dependent_name column. What is Dependent_name called?
questions.explanation: A weak entity's partial key (discriminator) distinguishes instances only in combination with the owner entity's primary key, here Emp_ssn + Dependent_name.

questions.question: A diagram shows a three-pronged fork symbol at the 'many' end of every relationship and bar or circle symbols at the 'one' end. Which ER notation uses these symbols?
questions.explanation: Crow's foot (Martin/Information Engineering) notation represents cardinality with a crow's foot for 'many' and bars/circles for mandatory and optional 'one'.

questions.question: EMPLOYEE has the attribute Languages_spoken, and a single employee may list several languages. Under ER-to-relational mapping, where must the language values be stored?
questions.explanation: Each multivalued attribute is mapped to its own relation whose primary key is (owner key, attribute value), so storing languages inside EMPLOYEE would violate 1NF.

questions.question: LOAN is a weak entity that cannot exist without its owner CUSTOMER; the relationship tying each loan to the customer who identifies it has a special name. What is it called?
questions.explanation: A weak entity is always linked to its owner through an identifying relationship; together with the owner's key it provides the weak entity's identification.

questions.question: In the recursive SUPERVISION relationship on EMPLOYEE, the diagram annotates one participation 'Supervisor' and the other 'Supervisee' to clarify who plays which part. What are these annotations called?
questions.explanation: Role names are required on recursive relationships because the same entity type participates twice; without them the two participations cannot be told apart.

questions.question: A model must express a BANK_ACCOUNT supertype with SAVINGS and CHECKING subtypes, plus an ACCOUNT_HOLDER set drawn from either PERSON or COMPANY. Plain ER cannot express this — which extended model is required?
questions.explanation: The Enhanced ER model adds subclasses/superclasses, specialization, generalization, and categories — none of which exist in basic ER notation.

questions.question: ACCOUNT_HOLDER must contain members that are either PERSON entities or COMPANY entities — a subclass drawn from the union of two different superclasses. Which EER construct models this subclass?
questions.explanation: A category (union type) is a subclass whose members are selected from the union of multiple distinct superclasses, unlike a regular subclass with one superclass.

questions.question: An ER model treats the ENROLLS relationship between STUDENT and SECTION as a higher-level entity so that it can itself participate in a relationship with EXAM. Which EER construct lets a relationship participate in other relationships?
questions.explanation: Aggregation abstracts a relationship into a higher-level entity, allowing it to take part in further relationships.

questions.question: When mapping a specialization of EMPLOYEE into SECRETARY and TECHNICIAN, the designer keeps the EMPLOYEE relation and adds one relation per subclass containing only the primary key of EMPLOYEE plus that subclass's own attributes. Which of the standard specialization-mapping options (8A, 8B, or 8C) is this?
questions.explanation: Option 8A creates a superclass relation plus one relation per subclass holding the superclass key and specialized attributes; 8B gives each subclass all superclass attributes, and 8C uses a single relation with a type attribute.

questions.question: A UML class diagram shows ENGINE as part of CAR using a filled diamond, meaning an ENGINE cannot exist independently of its CAR. Which stronger form of aggregation does the filled diamond denote?
questions.explanation: A filled diamond denotes composition, where the part's lifetime is bound to the whole; an open diamond denotes shared aggregation.

questions.question: Decomposing a ternary relationship SUPPLY(SUPPLIER, PART, PROJECT) into three binary relationships and joining them back produces rows that never occurred in the original relationship. What are these phantom result rows called?
questions.explanation: Joining the binary projections generates spurious tuples, showing the ternary relationship cannot always be decomposed losslessly.

questions.question: In (min, max) structural-constraint notation, each employee must be assigned to at least 2 and at most 4 projects. What pair is written next to EMPLOYEE's participation in the WORKS_ON relationship?
questions.explanation: The (min, max) notation specifies structural constraints on participation; (2, 4) requires each employee to appear in 2 to 4 relationship instances.
